scale.label: 25 µm detail
scale.note: Tier canonical metre length 2.528e-5 m. The nominal label is 25 µm. The model targets that length as the selected Turing wavelength on the cap wall.

evolutionary_history.what_changes_at_this_scale: The developmental predecessor is the unpatterned apex of the same Holocene cell: the homogeneous Brusselator state is stable below one wavelength and under equal diffusion. At this scale a 202.24 µm patch of cap wall holds eight axial pigment ridges at λ = 25.28 µm. Eleven periodic copies tile a young cap of margin radius 354 µm (88 ridges). There is no successor chronospecies; later cap expansion adds ridges at the same wavenumber. This is not the organism-scale whorl spacing of sibling slot 192.

equations.pde: du/dt = div(D_u grad u) + A - (B+1)u + u^2 v; dv/dt = div(D_v grad v) + B u - u^2 v
equations.turing_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
equations.boundary_conditions: periodic on the unwrapped cap-wall patch; the face-on render tiles that periodic field around the disk

parameters.note: D and B are chosen so the fastest linear mode sits on the 25.28 µm tier length. The axial/hoop ratio is reconstructed for this detail scale; Dumais & Harrison 2000 do not publish that number.

empirical_claims: Dumais & Harrison 2000: of mechanical buckling, reaction-diffusion, and Ca2+-cytoskeleton models, experiments on Acetabularia whorls favour reaction-diffusion along the membrane.
Harrison, Graham & Lakowski 1988: whorl pattern is preceded by an annular calcium pattern; spacing depends on extracellular calcium.
Holloway & Harrison 2007: a Brusselator on a growing surface produces tip growth and whorled branching.

This slot's 25.28 µm figure is the tier-4 detail length, not a spacing quoted from those papers. Onset λ under the nominal diffusivities is 22.67 µm; the fastest mode is 25.43 µm; the saturated patch peak is about 25.08 µm.
